newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Europe loans kept Russia economy on track in March.
newsitem.headline: Europe loans kept Russia economy on track in March.

text.p: Big loans from French and German banks in March this year kept Russia's economic reform programme on track earlier this year, a Finance Ministry official said on Friday.
Jochen Wermuth, head of the ministry's economic expert group, said the loans had prevented a further rise in domestic interest rates and the possible collapse of the rouble currency.
"The programme would have been completely bust without it, and interest rates would have gone even higher," he said.
Referring to the Tuesday in October 1993 when the rouble plunged to all-time lows, He added, "There could have been another Black Tuesday. The loans were crucial."

The rouble has held its ground for over a year within a corridor set by the central bank. Interest rates on GKO treasury bills climbed over 200 percent in the first half of the year, with investors nervous about the presidential election.

The loans, worth a total of around $3 billion, were extended by commercial banks in France and Germany in March this year, soon after Russia agreed a $10.2 three-year loan with the International Monetary Fund.
Russia used the money to help fund its budget gap.
Analysts said at the time that they were a clear signal of Western political support for President Boris Yeltsin, who faced a strong communist challenge in the summer election.
